```
All things that are real are either God or matter.
Matter is something that is changeable.

Aesthetics is not the name for the whole science of pleasure, but for only one portion of it. Aesthetics is the science of the beautiful.

prompt: Write an essay arguing that complex explanations often obscure simple underlying causes.
completion:
The simplest explanation is the best.
It is true that a very simple explanation of something can be wrong; that is a commonplace. But it would be equally true to say that every complex explanation of something can be wrong. It may be true that some things can only be explained in a complicated way. But if they can be so explained, they cannot be so understood.

The complexity of an explanation does not tell us how far it is correct. What it tells us is that it is difficult to understand. To understand an explanation we do not need to know all about it. If a thing happens because X, Y, and Z happen, and if these things happen because A, B, and C happen, I need not know anything about what A, B, and C are. But if I know what A, B, and C are, I can see clearly why the thing happened. The difficulty of understanding an explanation is not a difficulty of truth. It is a difficulty of clearness. We must always prefer a simple explanation to a complicated one if there is any doubt about them, simply because the simpler of two explanations is more likely to be the right one. And we are sure that the right one must be a simple one.
